correctness.rationale: For every admissible pair (n,k), the set of equidistant witnesses is exactly the nonresolving obstruction. The Johnson intersection metric gives E_r(n,k)=sum_j C(r,j)^2 C(n-2r,k-2j). A fully proved coefficientwise Vandermonde lemma shows E_r<=E_1 when n>2r. The only remaining n=2r case forces complementary half-subsets; exact binomial inequalities settle all odd and even half-sizes with only (4,2) and (8,4) exceptions. Direct exact vertex-pair enumeration and an independently expressed parameter-level formula confirm finite tests, with no inference from finite data to infinity.

originality.rationale: The 2013 generic resolving-number obstruction formula and 2012 Johnson resolving-set constructions do not imply a closed extremizer classification in the Johnson scheme. The 2021 Johnson distance-equalizer work has the opposite witness requirement, while the 2022 threshold study handles other graph families. The new coefficientwise comparison proves the all-parameter Johnson formula and isolates two antipodal anomalies; searches disclosed no earlier covering statement.

value.rationale: The resolving number is a worst-case robustness threshold for any collection of distance landmarks on a central family of fixed-cardinality set graphs. The complete exact two-parameter formula, with two unexpected antipodal exceptions, is motivated by graph metric identification and is mathematically more informative than an isolated census or a generic max formula. Its nontrivial binomial coefficient inequality makes the classification structural.
